3. Melamine layout and cutting plan Each panel is numbered by the sheet it is cut from. Full sheets S1 to S1 go in whole; the cut pieces sit at the corners. S2 gives the 2000 strip for the front right. S3 gives the 1600 strip for the left return. S4 gives the 1600 strip for the right return.

4. Suggested Build Sequence Build left to right as seen from the mall: left return, front, right return. 1 Check the truck. Before leaving, check the truck against the materials form to make sure all the material was loaded, including the 2 spare sheets. 2 Arrive and secure the area. Sign in with centre management. Set up barrier tape and the bollard around the work zone. Lay the dust suppression. 3 Set out the hoarding limit. Mark both ends of the lease line and measure 1600 out from each. Snap the 6000 front line parallel to the shopfront. 4 Mark the entry. Measure 2400 from the left end of the front line and mark a 1600 opening (2400 to 4000). 5 Stand the Titan uprights. 6 uprights, each one at a joint between two sheets (never in the middle of a sheet), including one each side of the entry, 2 counterweights on each (weight matrix for 1.2 m). They are marked on the melamine layout. Plus 1 spare upright (10%), not placed on the layout, with its 2 counterweights. 14 counterweights are sent (7 x 2). 6 Frame the walls. Fix the 70 x 45 MGP 10 studs (1.2 m) so every melamine joint lands on a stud. Frame the entry with 2 x 1.2 m and 4 x 2.3 m door studs and a head at 1200. Note: the 4 x 2.3 m door studs are on the form as usual; whether a 1.2 m kiosk needs them is still being checked with the boss. 7 Fix the 2400 x 1200 sheets, laid horizontally. Left return S3 (1600, at the corner); front left S1; front right S2 (2000, at the corner); right return S4 (1600, at the corner). 8 Hang the doors. One 2340 door cut in half: two 800 x 1200 leaves on 4 hinges, metal plates and deadbolt. Check they close and lock. 9 Finish. White tape on every vertical joint, black skirting tape along the base, screw covers, anti-tampers, 6 warning stickers, paint touch-ups. 10 Hand over. Clean up, remove the barrier, photograph each side, complete the installation certificate and sign INST CHK. 5. Site checks Confirm before fixing anything; update the drawings if any differ. [ ] The front measures 6000. [ ] The ceiling is above 1200 along the whole run. [ ] The entry starts 2400 from the left end of the front. [ ] The 1600 returns leave the walkway centre management requires. [ ] Nothing is fixed to the shopfront or floor; the Titan counterweights hold the hoarding. 6. Materials form follows on the next page.

How this price is worked out  Pacific Fair hoardings are charged per lineal metre (lm) under the agreed BSG Commercial Internal Hoarding Schedule of Rates for GPT - Pacific Fair 25-26.  The lineal metres are the full hoarding run, which includes the returns and sides as well as the front: 1,600 + 6,000 + 1,600 = 9,200 mm = 9.2 lm.  The hoarding is 1,200 mm high, so it falls in the 1.2 m high kiosk band at $115.00 per lm (ex GST). The rate rises with height because taller hoardings need more melamine, more counterweights per upright and more labour to install safely.  The run is shorter than the 15 lm minimum charge for this hoarding type, so 15 lm is charged.  15 lm x $115.00 = $1,725.00 ex GST, plus GST at 10%. 4. What is included  Supply, delivery, installation and removal of the TITAN free-standing hoarding system.  Structural engineering certification to AS4687 (pre-engineered certified hoarding).  16 mm white melamine boards with white taped joints and black skirting tape along the bottom.  One set of double doors, opening 2340 mm high x 1600 mm wide, with barrel bolt (deadbolt lock provided by Pacific Fair).  Free-standing installation: nothing is fixed to the centre's finishes, so there is no damage and no make-good work when the hoarding is removed.  Hoarding drawing for approval (attached).  Hoarding on site for up to 6 months before further charges apply.
